source.title: ErrorReporter logs every error at error level when Sentry is not configured

labels.name: status:in-linear
labels.description: Issue or PR is now in Linear

source.body:
### Bug Description

Without a Sentry DSN, `ErrorReporter.defaultReport` (`packages/core/src/errors/error-reporter.ts`) logs every reported error and every error in its `cause` chain with `logger.error`. It ignores the error's `level` and the `level` in the reporting options, so `ErrorReporter.warn()` also ends up at error level.

n8n already gives errors a level: `UserError` is `info`, `NodeOperationError` / `NodeApiError` / `OperationalError` are `warning`, and `UnexpectedError` is `error`. With Sentry enabled, `beforeSend` drops `warning` and `info`. Without Sentry, the same errors are logged as `level: "error"`.

Because of this, a self-hosted instance that alerts on error-level logs gets alerted for user mistakes in Code nodes and for 4xx responses from third-party APIs. On our instance, more than half of the error-level log lines in one week came from a `TypeError` in a single workflow's Code node.

Log output from the steps below:

```
{"level":"error","message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'channel') [line 2]","metadata":{"file":"error-reporter.js","function":"defaultReport",...}}
{"level":"error","message":"Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'channel') [line 2]\nTypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'channel')\n    at VmCodeWrapper ...","metadata":{"file":"error-reporter.js","function":"defaultReport",...}}
{"level":"error","message":"The resource you are requesting could not be found","metadata":{"file":"error-reporter.js","function":"defaultReport",...}}
{"level":"error","message":"404 - ...\nAxiosError: Request failed with status code 404 ...","metadata":{"file":"error-reporter.js","function":"defaultReport",...}}
```

The code is the same on `master` today. #42905 adds level filtering, but only for redacted executions.

A possible fix: in `defaultReport`, pick the level the same way the Sentry path does (`options.level` if it is set and not `error`, otherwise the error's own `level`, otherwise `error`), and log the whole cause chain with the matching logger method. We run this as a patch on our instance. Since this is under `packages/core`, we'd like to check whether you'd accept this approach before opening a PR with a regression test in `error-reporter.test.ts`.

### To Reproduce

1. `docker run -p 5678:5678 -e N8N_LOG_FORMAT=json n8nio/n8n:2.46.6` (no Sentry DSN)
2. Create and activate a workflow: Webhook → Code (Run Once for Each Item) with `const x = undefined; return {json: {a: x.channel}};`
3. Create and activate a workflow: Webhook → HTTP Request to `http://localhost:5678/rest/nonexistent` (returns 404)
4. Call both production webhook URLs
5. See the container logs

### Expected behavior

The Code node error (`UserError`, level `info`) is logged at `info`, and the 404 (`NodeApiError`, level `warning`) is logged at `warn`. Only errors with level `error` or `fatal` are logged at `error`.

### Debug Info

Official Docker image `n8nio/n8n:2.46.6`, default settings except `N8N_LOG_FORMAT=json`, no Sentry DSN. Also seen in production with PostgreSQL and task runners in external mode.

### Operating System

Docker Hardened Images / Alpine Linux v3.24 (official image)

### n8n Version

2.46.6

### Node.js Version

v26.12.1

### Database

SQLite (default)

### Execution mode

main (default)

### Hosting

self hosted
